categories.name: Start here
categories.about: The bundle in ten minutes: what it is, first apps, and a few lines that do a lot.

demos.label: What is an Immediate GUI
demos.text:
With [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), your GUI code is **simple and direct**: no widget trees,
no callbacks, no state synchronization. You call functions to create widgets, and they return the current
value. That's it.
demos.summary: With [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), your GUI code is **simple and direct**: no widget trees, no callbacks, no state synchronization.

demos.label: Hello world, in two lines
demos.text:
[ImmApp](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/hello-imgui-immapp/) opens the window, runs the loop, and calls
your GUI function at every frame: `immapp.run(gui)` is all it takes. Add widgets to that function, and you have an
app. The C++ version is three lines.
demos.summary: [ImmApp](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/hello-imgui-immapp/) opens the window, runs the loop, and calls your GUI function at every frame: `immapp.run(gui)` is all it takes.

demos.label: A parametric curve
demos.text:
Turn the knobs, or click **Random**: the curve follows at once. At every frame, the GUI function draws the plot with
[ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) and the knobs with
[imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs), and reads their values right there. No callbacks, no widget
objects: that is the [immediate mode](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/intro/imm-gui/).
demos.summary: Turn the knobs, or click **Random**: the curve follows at once.

demos.label: A plot and markdown, in a few lines
demos.text:
A cosine wave moves in an [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) plot, under a text written in
[markdown](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/addons/text-markdown/). Both are add-ons, activated in one call:
`immapp.run(gui, with_implot=True, with_markdown=True)`. A good start for a small app.
demos.summary: A cosine wave moves in an [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) plot, under a text written in [markdown](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/addons/text-markdown/).

demos.label: Assets and add-ons
demos.text:
Load images and icons from your [assets folder](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-assets/), and use
two add-ons: markdown and ImPlot. A markdown editor with a live preview, and a pie chart whose values you can drag.
Tick **More info** under each part to see how it is done. The add-ons are activated with `immapp.AddOnsParams`.
demos.summary: Load images and icons from your [assets folder](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-assets/), and use two add-ons: markdown and ImPlot.

demos.label: A beating heart
demos.text:
A heart curve drawn with [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) beats at the rate set by a knob from
[imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs). A few lines of Python: a parametric curve, scaled by a pulse
at each frame. Turn the knobs to change the heart rate, or its thickness.
demos.summary: A heart curve drawn with [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) beats at the rate set by a knob from [imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs).

demos.label: Butterfly effect, in a few lines
demos.text:
Two trajectories of the [Lorenz system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system) start almost at the same point,
then drift apart: chaos in action. Drawn in 3D with [ImPlot3D](https://github.com/brenocq/implot3d). Sliders change
the system's parameters and the gap between the two starting points; Reset starts them over.
demos.summary: Two trajectories of the [Lorenz system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system) start almost at the same point, then drift apart: chaos in action.

categories.name: Interactive manuals
categories.about: Dear ImGui, ImPlot, ImPlot3D and ImAnim: all their features, section by section, with the code beside.

demos.label: Dear ImGui: the interactive manual
demos.text:
Every widget and feature of [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), section by section, with the Python and
C++ code of each beside it. From [Dear ImGui Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/), the interactive
manual for Dear ImGui and its libraries.
demos.summary: Every widget and feature of [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), section by section, with the Python and C++ code of each beside it.

demos.label: ImPlot: the interactive manual
demos.text:
Every kind of plot of [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot), section by section, with the code of each beside
it. Lines, scatter, bars, heatmaps, histograms, real-time plots and more, in Python and C++. From
[Dear ImGui Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/), the interactive manual for Dear ImGui and its libraries.
demos.summary: Every kind of plot of [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot), section by section, with the code of each beside it.

demos.label: ImPlot3D: the interactive manual
demos.text:
The 3D plots of [ImPlot3D](https://github.com/brenocq/implot3d), section by section, with the code of each beside it.
Lines, scatter, surfaces, meshes and more, in Python and C++. From
[Dear ImGui Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/), the interactive manual for Dear ImGui and its libraries.
demos.summary: The 3D plots of [ImPlot3D](https://github.com/brenocq/implot3d), section by section, with the code of each beside it.

demos.label: ImAnim: the interactive manual
demos.text:
The animations of [ImAnim](https://github.com/SoufianeKHIAT/ImAnim), section by section, with the code of each beside
it. Tweens, easings, oscillators, delays, callbacks, stagger, loops and chains, in Python and C++. From
[Dear ImGui Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/), the interactive manual for Dear ImGui and its libraries.
demos.summary: The animations of [ImAnim](https://github.com/SoufianeKHIAT/ImAnim), section by section, with the code of each beside it.

categories.name: Build an app
categories.about: Layouts, docking, backgrounds, fonts, testing: what a real application needs.

demos.label: Resizable panels with child windows
demos.text: Learn how to create resizable adjacent panels, using child windows.
demos.summary: Learn how to create resizable adjacent panels, using child windows.

demos.label: Dockable windows
demos.text:
[Hello ImGui](https://github.com/pthom/hello_imgui) provides a **docking** system: define named dock spaces,
then assign windows to them.
Windows can be dragged, tabbed, and rearranged by the user.
demos.summary: [Hello ImGui](https://github.com/pthom/hello_imgui) provides a **docking** system: define named dock spaces, then assign windows to them.

demos.label: A full app: docking, fonts, logs
demos.summary: A template for a real application, built with [Hello ImGui](https://pthom.github.io/hello_imgui/): copy it and start from there.

demos.label: Custom 3D background (OpenGL)
demos.text:
Draw anything behind your GUI with OpenGL: here, an animated sea whose waves and colors you can tune. The [Seascape
shader](https://www.shadertoy.com/view/Ms2SD1) is by Alexander Alekseev (TDM, 2014). Hello ImGui calls
`runner_params.callbacks.custom_background` at each frame, before the GUI: that is where it draws, with OpenGL
([PyOpenGL](https://pypi.org/project/PyOpenGL/) in Python).
demos.summary: Draw anything behind your GUI with OpenGL: here, an animated sea whose waves and colors you can tune.

demos.label: Power save when idle
demos.text:
When nothing happens, [Hello ImGui](https://pthom.github.io/hello_imgui/) lowers the frame rate to spare the CPU:
after 3 seconds, the live plot and the spinner become choppy. Content that changes on its own says so with
`hello_imgui.set_item_is_live()`, and keeps the full speed while it is visible. The idling settings are global.
demos.summary: When nothing happens, [Hello ImGui](https://pthom.github.io/hello_imgui/) lowers the frame rate to spare the CPU: after 3 seconds, the live plot and the spinner become choppy.

demos.label: Chinese and other non-Latin fonts
demos.text:
The bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic only: other scripts show up as `???`. The fix: load a font that has
the glyphs you need, first, so that it becomes the default font. This demo shows how, with [Noto Sans
SC](https://fonts.google.com/noto/specimen/Noto+Sans+SC): download it, and the demo's sample lines come alive.
demos.summary: The bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic only: other scripts show up as `???`.

demos.label: Drag and drop
demos.text:
Drag a name onto another button to copy it, move it, or swap the two: the radio buttons pick the mode. Each button is
both a drag source and a drop target. Adapted from the drag and drop section of the [Dear ImGui
demo](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/blob/master/imgui_demo.cpp).
demos.summary: Drag a name onto another button to copy it, move it, or swap the two: the radio buttons pick the mode.

demos.label: Command palette
demos.text:
A searchable list of commands, as in VS Code: press **Ctrl+Shift+P** (**Cmd+Shift+P** on macOS). Type a few letters
to filter it. One command changes the theme in two steps, another writes to the log below. Learn how to register
commands and their callbacks with [imgui-command-palette](https://github.com/hnOsmium0001/imgui-command-palette).
demos.summary: A searchable list of commands, as in VS Code: press **Ctrl+Shift+P** (**Cmd+Shift+P** on macOS).

demos.label: Test engine
demos.text:
Watch a [ImGui Test Engine](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui_test_engine) drive the mouse and the keyboard:
it clicks buttons, types text, etc., and checks the results.
For scripted runs on top of it (automated tests, pictures, an AI agent at the mouse), see the `immapp.testing` demo.
See the [test engine doc](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/test-engine/).
demos.summary: Watch a [ImGui Test Engine](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui_test_engine) drive the mouse and the keyboard: it clicks buttons, types text, etc., and checks the results.

demos.label: immapp.testing: scripted runs
demos.text:
Easy automated tests with `immapp.testing`, a thin layer on the test engine: a script drives the app, then exits.
The test engine demo shows the engine itself. Here, a test function drives the GUI (it clicks, moves a slider, opens
a header) and captures a picture at each step; `immapp.testing.run()` starts the app, runs the test, then exits.
The same recipe gives documentation pictures, and lets an AI agent see and drive the app it writes, with nobody at
the mouse (the bundle's screenshot skills are built on it).
See the [test engine doc](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/test-engine/).
demos.summary: Easy automated tests with `immapp.testing`, a thin layer on the test engine: a script drives the app, then exits.

categories.name: Library tours
categories.about: The libraries in the bundle: full demos, widget tours, showcases.

demos.label: Themes and theme tweaking
demos.text:
Pick a complete look for your app, then fine-tune its colors, rounding and spacing. The complete
looks come from [Hello ImGui](https://github.com/pthom/hello_imgui).
demos.summary: Pick a complete look for your app, then fine-tune its colors, rounding and spacing.

demos.label: Knobs, toggles, spinners and more
demos.text:
Knobs, toggle switches, spinners, a command palette, a dock-like cool bar: widgets beyond Dear ImGui's own. They come
from the libraries in the bundle: [imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs),
[imgui_toggle](https://github.com/cmdwtf/imgui_toggle), [imspinner](https://github.com/dalerank/imspinner),
[imgui-command-palette](https://github.com/hnOsmium0001/imgui-command-palette) and ImCoolBar. Also file dialogs: the
native ones ([portable-file-dialogs](https://github.com/samhocevar/portable-file-dialogs)), and
[ImFileDialog](https://github.com/pthom/ImFileDialog), drawn with ImGui.
demos.summary: Knobs, toggle switches, spinners, a command palette, a dock-like cool bar: widgets beyond Dear ImGui's own.

demos.label: Markdown tour
demos.text:
Markdown rendered in an ImGui window: styled text, tables, code, images, math, diagrams, admonitions and more. Each
section shows its source, ready to copy. The page is a document: a table of contents, a search, headings that fold.
demos.summary: Markdown rendered in an ImGui window: styled text, tables, code, images, math, diagrams, admonitions and more.

demos.label: Markdown: a document with a table of contents and a search
demos.text:
Markdown as a document: a table of contents beside it, links between its sections, and a search (Ctrl+F). Several
renders and a section of widgets (a plot) share them, in one scroll area. The search also finds the text of the code
blocks and of the collapsed sections. The headings fold.
demos.summary: Markdown as a document: a table of contents beside it, links between its sections, and a search (Ctrl+F).

demos.label: Code editor
demos.text:
A code editor widget, with syntax highlighting, multiple cursors, a diff view, filters, annotations and context menus.
Each tab shows one feature, and a checkbox shows its source. The editor is
[ImGuiColorTextEdit](https://github.com/goossens/ImGuiColorTextEdit), by Johan A. Goossens.
demos.summary: A code editor widget, with syntax highlighting, multiple cursors, a diff view, filters, annotations and context menus.

demos.label: Log window
demos.text:
A log window for your app, with four levels: debug, info, warning and error. Call `hello_imgui.log()` anywhere, and
show the window with `hello_imgui.log_gui()`. Its colors follow the theme. Adapted from
[ImGuiAl](https://github.com/leiradel/ImGuiAl).
demos.summary: A log window for your app, with four levels: debug, info, warning and error.

demos.label: Terminal
demos.text:
A real shell in an ImGui widget: type commands, scroll back through the history, select and copy. The shell runs
behind a pseudo-terminal (macOS and Linux), [pyte](https://github.com/selectel/pyte) parses its VT100 output, and
`imgui_bundle.imgui_terminal.TerminalView` draws it. A standalone version, with more comments:
`demos_terminal/demo_terminal_pyte.py`.
demos.summary: A real shell in an ImGui widget: type commands, scroll back through the history, select and copy.

demos.label: ImmVision: display and inspect
demos.text:
Two ways to show an image (a NumPy array in Python, a cv::Mat in C++). `immvision.image_display_resizable()` draws
it, and you drag its corner to resize it. `immvision.image()` adds the inspection tools: zoom with the mouse wheel until the pixel values
show, pan by dragging, and a button at the bottom right corner opens the settings (colormaps, channels, values).
demos.summary: Two ways to show an image (a NumPy array in Python, a cv::Mat in C++).

demos.label: ImmVision: the inspector
demos.text:
Call `immvision.inspector_add_image()` anywhere, for example at each step of an image processing algorithm. Then
`immvision.inspector_show()` shows all the collected images, with the zoom, the pan and the pixel inspection of
`immvision.image()`. Here, two photos at startup; on the desktop, a button adds images of every depth and channel
count.
demos.summary: Call `immvision.inspector_add_image()` anywhere, for example at each step of an image processing algorithm.

demos.label: ImmVision: images that zoom together
demos.text:
Image params that share a `zoom_key` follow each other: pan or zoom one image, and the others move with it. Here, a
photo and its three color channels. Pan by dragging, zoom with the mouse wheel. The image is read with OpenCV
(`pip install imgui-bundle[imgproc]`).
demos.summary: Image params that share a `zoom_key` follow each other: pan or zoom one image, and the others move with it.

demos.label: ImmVision: image processing, tuned live
demos.text:
A Sobel filter on a photo: change the blur, the derivative's order and its orientation, and the result updates at
once. The original and the filtered image share a zoom key, so they pan and zoom together; the options panel of the
filtered image applies colormaps. A button downloads a random photo. The processing is OpenCV's
(`pip install imgui-bundle[imgproc]`), the display ImmVision's.
demos.summary: A Sobel filter on a photo: change the blur, the derivative's order and its orientation, and the result updates at once.

demos.label: Node editor: a color mixer
demos.text:
Colors flow through a small graph: pick two colors, mix them, and see the result in the swatches. Each link is drawn
in the color it carries. A first graph with [imgui-node-editor](https://github.com/thedmd/imgui-node-editor): the
nodes, pins and links that the app owns, and how the user edits them.
demos.summary: Colors flow through a small graph: pick two colors, mix them, and see the result in the swatches.

demos.label: Node editor: an image pipeline
demos.text:
An image flows through a graph of filters, and each node shows its result. Change a parameter, and the nodes
downstream follow at once. The patterns of [imgui-node-editor](https://github.com/thedmd/imgui-node-editor) for a
real app: typed pins, links refused with a reason, a node created by dropping a link in empty space, menus, a group.
demos.summary: An image flows through a graph of filters, and each node shows its result.

demos.label: ImGuizmo: a 3D gizmo
demos.text:
Move, rotate and scale cubes with a gizmo, as in a 3D editor. Pick the operation and the mode (local or world) in the
editor panel, drag the gizmo's handles, and turn the view with the cube at the top right corner. The gizmo is
[ImGuizmo](https://github.com/CedricGuillemet/ImGuizmo); the camera matrices are a few lines of plain Python.
demos.summary: Move, rotate and scale cubes with a gizmo, as in a 3D editor.

demos.label: NanoVG: the full demo
demos.text:
The demo of [NanoVG](https://github.com/memononen/nanovg), a vector drawing library: shapes, gradients, text, images.
Drawn each frame behind the GUI, or into a framebuffer that an ImGui image shows. The scene follows the mouse, and a
checkbox blows it up.
demos.summary: The demo of [NanoVG](https://github.com/memononen/nanovg), a vector drawing library: shapes, gradients, text, images.

demos.label: NanoVG: a beating heart
demos.text:
A heart drawn with [NanoVG](https://github.com/memononen/nanovg) beats in an ImGui image. NanoVG is a vector drawing
library; the drawing goes into a framebuffer that the image shows, and a color picker changes the heart's color. The
pattern for any NanoVG drawing inside a GUI: `nvg_imgui.render_nvg_to_frame_buffer()`.
demos.summary: A heart drawn with [NanoVG](https://github.com/memononen/nanovg) beats in an ImGui image.

demos.label: Terminal: several shells in tabs
demos.text:
Real shells in a tab bar, each behind a pseudo-terminal. Type, scroll the history, select and copy, and open more
terminals with the "+" tab. This file is the application only: the widget is `imgui_bundle.imgui_terminal`'s
`TerminalView`, fed by a `LocalShellTransport`. Needs `pip install "imgui-bundle[terminal]"` (pyte), on macOS or Linux.
demos.summary: Real shells in a tab bar, each behind a pseudo-terminal.

demos.label: Terminal over SSH
demos.text:
The same terminal widget, fed by an SSH channel instead of a local shell. With [paramiko](https://www.paramiko.org):
the shape of a shell on a server or a robot, from a desktop GUI. By default it connects to localhost as you, through
the SSH agent; edit the host and the user in the file. Needs `pip install "imgui-bundle[terminal]" paramiko`.
demos.summary: The same terminal widget, fed by an SSH channel instead of a local shell.

demos.label: Terminal over a websocket
demos.text:
The same terminal widget, its bytes carried by a websocket to a pty bridge server. The demo starts the bridge
(`pty_bridge_server.py`); replace it by a shell on a robot, a server or a container, and the GUI stays the same.
Needs `pip install "imgui-bundle[terminal]" websockets`.
demos.summary: The same terminal widget, its bytes carried by a websocket to a pty bridge server.

categories.name: Python specifics
categories.about: Async, Matplotlib, Pydantic, context managers, and pure Python backends.

demos.label: Context managers (imgui_ctx)
demos.text:
In Python, `with imgui_ctx.begin("Window"):` replaces a `begin()` / `end()` pair, and the `end()` can no longer be
forgotten. The same exists for child windows, menus, popups, tables, tabs, fonts and styles, and for ImPlot with
`implot_ctx`. Open a section to try it and read its code. See the [Python
tips](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-tips/).
demos.summary: In Python, `with imgui_ctx.begin("Window"):` replaces a `begin()` / `end()` pair, and the `end()` can no longer be forgotten.

demos.label: Run code alongside the GUI (async)
demos.text:
The GUI runs as an [asyncio](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html) task, while a Python loop keeps
computing. The window shows both rates: the GUI's frames per second, and the loop's computations per second. The loop
yields with `await asyncio.sleep(0)` to share the event loop. See [async
support](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-async/).
demos.summary: The GUI runs as an [asyncio](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html) task, while a Python loop keeps computing.

demos.label: A GUI beside a Jupyter notebook
demos.text: At 60 or 120 frames per second, a live GUI beside your Jupyter notebook while the cells run. In async mode (`immapp.nb.start()`), another cell keeps computing, as fast as it can, between the frames: stream data into a plot, or train a model and tune it while it learns. The page explains both modes; its video trains a neural network live, its learning rate on a slider.
demos.summary: At 60 or 120 frames per second, a live GUI beside your Jupyter notebook while the cells run.

demos.label: Control the GLFW window
demos.text:
`glfw_utils.glfw_window_hello_imgui()` returns the [GLFW](https://www.glfw.org) window that Hello ImGui created. With
it, any function of [pyGLFW](https://github.com/FlorianRhiem/pyGLFW) works on your app's window. Here, buttons
maximize, restore, minimize or center it, a slider sets its opacity, and another button makes it ask for attention in
the taskbar.
demos.summary: `glfw_utils.glfw_window_hello_imgui()` returns the [GLFW](https://www.glfw.org) window that Hello ImGui created.

demos.label: Matplotlib figures
demos.text:
`imgui_fig.fig()` shows a [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org) figure as an image in the GUI. On the left, an animated
sine wave, redrawn at each frame, with a slider for its amplitude. On the right, a static figure, drawn once. Handy to
reuse existing Matplotlib code; for fast interactive plots, prefer [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot).
demos.summary: `imgui_fig.fig()` shows a [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org) figure as an image in the GUI.

demos.label: Pydantic models
demos.text:
Save and load your app's settings with [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev), ImVec2 and colors included.
`ImVec2_Pydantic`, `ImVec4_Pydantic` and `ImColor_Pydantic` are the usual `ImVec2`, `ImVec4` and `ImColor`, usable as
fields of a Pydantic model. The demo shows such a model, turns it into JSON, validates it back, and checks that
nothing was lost.
demos.summary: Save and load your app's settings with [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev), ImVec2 and colors included.

demos.label: Python backends: GLFW, SDL, pyglet, pygame, wgpu
demos.text:
With a pure Python backend, you drive the full app loop. See
[Pure Python backends](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/pure-python-backend/). Unlike `immapp.run()`, there
is no Hello ImGui here: no DPI handling, themes or assets.
demos.summary: With a pure Python backend, you drive the full app loop.

categories.name: In the browser
categories.about: Deploy to the web, and use the browser's WebGL and WebAudio from Python.

demos.label: Minimal HTML page
demos.text: Dear ImGui Bundle apps can run entirely in the browser using [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org). The HTML file below is a **complete, self-contained app** in about 80 lines - no server, no build step.
demos.summary: Dear ImGui Bundle apps can run entirely in the browser using [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org).

demos.label: Touch screens (phones, tablets)
demos.text:
The gestures of a phone in the browser: a swipe, a tap, a long press, a pinch, the keyboard.
On a mobile or a tablet, Hello ImGui turns a finger into what its user expects: a swipe scrolls,
a tap clicks, a held finger opens a context menu, a pinch scales the app (its font), two fingers pan, and a keyboard button
appears next to a text field.
demos.summary: The gestures of a phone in the browser: a swipe, a tap, a long press, a pinch, the keyboard.

demos.label: WebGL shader as background
demos.text:
The [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), drawn by a fragment shader behind the GUI.
**Pyodide only:** this demo calls the browser's
[WebGL2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API) API directly, through Python's `js`
interop. On desktop, you would use PyOpenGL instead.
demos.summary: The [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), drawn by a fragment shader behind the GUI.

demos.label: WebGL / OpenGL custom background
demos.text:
One source file, two platforms: a shader behind the GUI, with OpenGL on desktop and WebGL in the browser. The
shader is the famous "Seascape" from [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/view/Ms2SD1), by Alexander
Alekseev. In the browser, the app runs with [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org).
demos.summary: One source file, two platforms: a shader behind the GUI, with OpenGL on desktop and WebGL in the browser.

demos.label: WebGL 3D cube rendered to a texture
demos.text:
A 3D cube drawn with [WebGL2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API) into a texture, and
shown in the GUI by `imgui.image()`. No copy between the GPU and the CPU at each frame.
demos.summary: A 3D cube drawn with [WebGL2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API) into a texture, and shown in the GUI by `imgui.image()`.

demos.label: WebAudio synthesizer
demos.text:
A small synthesizer written in Python: play the piano with the mouse or the computer keyboard, or let it play a
tune. Pick a waveform, add some echo, and watch the scope. **Pyodide only**: it plays through the browser's
[WebAudio API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Audio_API), via [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org)'s
`js` interop.
demos.summary: A small synthesizer written in Python: play the piano with the mouse or the computer keyboard, or let it play a tune.

categories.name: Interactive science
categories.about: Explorable lessons in physics, chaos and machine learning, built with the bundle.
categories.tip: Dear ImGui Bundle excels at real-time scientific visualization: 60 frames per second or more, even under load. These demos show it.

demos.label: Interactive exploration of the Mandelbrot set
demos.text:
Click a point of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) to see its [Julia
set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set). Fly to famous values of c, and zoom into both pictures: near
each point, the two sets look alike.
demos.summary: Click a point of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) to see its [Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set).

demos.label: A tiny neural network learns two spirals
demos.text:
Can 16 neurons tell two spirals apart? Watch a tiny [neural
network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning)) learn, live, as in the [TensorFlow
Playground](https://playground.tensorflow.org). Then read how it works, formula by formula, next to its numpy
code.
demos.summary: Can 16 neurons tell two spirals apart? Watch a tiny [neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning)) learn, live, as in the [TensorFlow Playground](https://playground.tensorflow.org).

demos.label: Simple harmonic motion
demos.text:
A mass on a spring, a pendulum, a vibrating string: they all follow the same equation. It is the equation of
[simple harmonic motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_harmonic_motion) (for the pendulum, at small
angles). Adjust the mass and the spring stiffness, and watch how the motion changes.
demos.summary: A mass on a spring, a pendulum, a vibrating string: they all follow the same equation.

demos.label: Double pendulum
demos.text:
A [double pendulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_pendulum) is a
[chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) system: tiny changes in its initial conditions lead to
wildly different trajectories. Drag the angles to set initial positions, then release and watch chaos unfold.
demos.summary: A [double pendulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_pendulum) is a [chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) system: tiny changes in its initial conditions lead to wildly different trajectories.

demos.label: Fourier epicycles
demos.text:
Any closed curve can be approximated by a sum of rotating circles (a [Fourier
series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series)). Adjust the number of circles to see how the
approximation improves.
demos.summary: Any closed curve can be approximated by a sum of rotating circles (a [Fourier series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series)).

demos.label: Boids (flocks)
demos.text:
A flock of birds emerges from three simple local rules, with no leader and no plan. Each bird stays apart
from its neighbors (**separation**), flies their way (**alignment**), and stays with them (**cohesion**).
This is the [boids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boids) model of Craig Reynolds (1986).
demos.summary: A flock of birds emerges from three simple local rules, with no leader and no plan.

demos.label: Logistic map
demos.text:
A very simple equation, and yet it can lead to wildly different behaviors, up to chaos. The [logistic
map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logistic_map), `x(n+1) = r * x(n) * (1 - x(n))`, models for example the
*growth of a population with limited resources*. Depending on r, it is stable, periodic (in 2-cycles,
4-cycles, etc), or chaotic. Let's explore this.
demos.summary: A very simple equation, and yet it can lead to wildly different behaviors, up to chaos.
